solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... an exam or test successfully
second meaning: what a quiz contestant says to decline a question

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it read as one puzzled remark; it is two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Succeeding in an exam is passing it, and a quiz player who cannot answer declines with the same word.

parts.note: cute means pleasantly attractive or endearing

explanation.surface: Someone finds a French way of speaking charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French accent' looks like a way of speaking, but it means a diacritic mark used in written French.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is the rising diacritic mark found over the e in French words like café.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: normal, usual, the norm
second meaning: a banner, as carried by a regiment

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for the usual or normal kind and a noun for a banner carried into battle.

clue.text: Worker in branch to the north frequently repeated phrase

indicators.note: the worker sits inside the reversed branch
in a down clue, going north means the word branch's synonym is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of a river or organisation
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An employee up a tree keeps saying the same thing over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: ARM read upwards gives MRA, and ANT goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or slogan chanted repeatedly, originally in Hindu and Buddhist meditation.

indicators.note: the rearranged motel goes round the letter for right
letters that are wrong are put into the wrong order, so the word motel is rearranged

explanation.surface: A motel has served the wrong red instead of the right one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges MOTEL to MELOT, and 'about' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the wine made from it, widely grown in Bordeaux.

clue.text: Short promotional piece gives confused impression

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the promotional word is chopped off

parts.note: a blurb is the promotional text on a book jacket

explanation.surface: A brief advert leaves its readers muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is something seen or remembered indistinctly, without clear outlines.

clue.text: Passenger, bank worker, embracing most of party

indicators.note: the bank worker hugs the shortened party inside itself

parts.note: a teller is a bank clerk at the counter

indicators.note: all but the final letter of the party word is used

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A passenger turns out to be a bank clerk who is clutching a party invitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passenger, bank worker' reads as a list of two people, but the bank worker is wordplay; only 'Passenger' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is someone on a journey, as a passenger is on a train or plane.

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
side is old British slang for a television channel, from 'switch over to the other side'

explanation.surface: Something is being broadcast live on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like an adjective about broadcasting, but it is the verb to dwell.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to have your home there, to dwell.

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or altered, so the letters of aunt are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative has prepared some fish for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish of the mackerel family, widely eaten.

clue.text: Skin condition irritates husband entertaining artist

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in a guest, so the artist goes inside

parts.note: nettles means annoys or irritates
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
H is the abbreviation for husband in family trees

explanation.surface: A rash irritates a husband who is hosting a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettle rash is urticaria, an itchy skin eruption like the sting of a nettle.

clue.text: Show the way in battle — advance

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

parts.note: second meaning: a margin ahead of rivals, as in having the advantage

explanation.surface: A commander must show the way when the army moves forward.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a military command, but the answer straddles 'battle' and 'advance'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead is to guide others by going in front of them.

clue.text: Radically new vat, a danger if misused

indicators.note: misused letters are put to the wrong use, so vat, a and danger are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a vat could be hazardous when handled wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde describes experimental art or ideas ahead of their time, a vanguard.

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Some people in opposition are unlike a sister, by implication pugnacious.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a female member of a religious order, addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Interesting story from one cadet at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters of one cadet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval cadet brings back an interesting tale from a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing or interesting account of a real incident.

indicators.note: the press word wraps around the Northern Ireland abbreviation

parts.note: to push is to press

explanation.surface: The newspapers report on discipline in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To discipline someone, in the sense of penalising them, is to punish them.

clue.text: Group of team members quarrel, losing heads in courtyard

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a squad is a group of players in a team
a wrangle is a long argument

explanation.surface: Players fall out in a courtyard and come to blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heads' beheads both words: SQUAD becomes QUAD and WRANGLE becomes RANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle is a four-sided courtyard enclosed by buildings, as in an Oxford college.

parts.note: cross means irritable or annoyed

explanation.surface: A grumpy cricket over, as if the bowling itself were in a mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' suggests the six-ball cricket over, but it is the preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Over and across both mean from one side to the other, as in going over the bridge.

clue.text: Cake consumed in Gaul, no end

indicators.note: the consumed word goes into the shortened Gaul
the final letter of Gaul is dropped

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A cake eaten in ancient France, the story never quite finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaul is the Roman name for ancient France, which fits a French cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Gâteau is the French word for a rich layered cake, used in English for creamy ones.

parts.note: cha is slang for tea, from Chinese

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of tree

explanation.surface: Some tea under a tree gets people talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to talk informally and at ease.

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd of people

explanation.surface: An instruction to gather a crowd together.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate a large quantity.

indicators.note: the departed word takes the drink inside it

parts.note: died means departed this life
brandy is an example of a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy has left after drinking brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispirited means having lost enthusiasm, low in spirits and dejected.

indicators.note: the last letter of the factory word is missing

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory

explanation.surface: An unfinished blueprint for a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scale drawing of a building seen from above.

clue.text: Said of country life all but past

indicators.note: everything except the word past is kept

parts.note: pastoral describes rural life and shepherds

explanation.surface: A remark about country life being a thing of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' here means except: the country word without PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, so an oral statement is one said aloud.

clue.text: He's bitter about a duke giving one an advantage

indicators.note: the letters of He's go around a and the duke abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
tart means sharp or bitter

explanation.surface: A sour man's remark about a duke getting a leg up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and D inside HES, giving HEADS.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an early lead given to a competitor, an edge over rivals.

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to put out a programme in plain English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual signal for an example, but it is plain anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means not difficult, straightforward to do.
